title: [FLINK-40295][docs] Document UDF metrics
body:
This is the fourth and final PR of the FLIP-485 implementation, split into a stack of small, independently reviewable PRs under the umbrella issue [FLINK-38071](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/FLINK-38071). Landing order:

| Step | Sub-task | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| PR-1 ✅ merged | [FLINK-40292](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/FLINK-40292) | `UdfMetrics` helper: registration, sampling, timing, exception counting ([#28878](https://github.com/apache/flink/pull/28878)) |
| PR-2 ✅ merged | [FLINK-40293](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/FLINK-40293) | Config options + sync scalar/table instrumentation ([#28879](https://github.com/apache/flink/pull/28879)) |
| PR-3 ✅ merged | [FLINK-40294](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/FLINK-40294) | Async scalar/table instrumentation ([#29007](https://github.com/apache/flink/pull/29007)) |
| **PR-4 (this PR)** | [FLINK-40295](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/FLINK-40295) | User-facing documentation |

## What is the purpose of the change

Documents the UDF metrics added by PR-1 to PR-3 on the metrics page, so users can find the two metrics, turn them on, understand what sampling does to the numbers, and see which functions are not covered.

## Brief change log

- Add a `UDF` subsection to the system metrics reference in `docs/ops/metrics.md`, listing `udfProcessingTime` (Histogram, nanoseconds) and `udfExceptionCount` (Counter) with the `Operator` scope and a `udf.<udf_name>` infix, following the page's scope/infix convention.
- Add a `UDF metrics` section after the state access latency and state size tracking sections, following their structure: how to enable it with `table.exec.udf-metric-enabled`, what `table.exec.udf-metric.sample-interval` controls, and the same performance warning.
- State the coverage explicitly: scalar and table functions called directly by a query, sync and async. Not covered are Python functions (they run in dedicated Python operators), process table functions, aggregate functions, functions registered through the deprecated `registerFunction` API, and the functions invoked internally by lookup joins, model prediction, and vector search. The last group matches the instrumentation in PR-2, where only the bridging call sites carry a metric name, and is asserted by `UdfMetricsITCase#testLookupJoinNotMetered`.
- The Chinese page carries the same English text.

The config option reference (`execution_config_configuration.html`) was already regenerated in PR-2.

## Verifying this change

This change is documentation only and has no test coverage. Each statement was checked against the merged code: the option keys and the default of 100 (`ExecutionConfigOptions`), the metric names, the `udf` group and the nanosecond unit (`UdfMetrics`), the covered call sites (`BridgingSqlFunctionCallGen` and the async correlate entry in `BridgingFunctionGenUtil`), and the operator-only registration (`UdfMetrics.register`).

## Does this pull request potentially affect one of the following parts:

  - Dependencies (does it add or upgrade a dependency): no
  - The public API, i.e., is any changed class annotated with `@Public(Evolving)`: no
  - The serializers: no
  - The runtime per-record code paths (performance sensitive): no
  - Anything that affects deployment or recovery: JobManager (and its components), Checkpointing, Kubernetes/Yarn, ZooKeeper: no
  - The S3 file system connector: no

## Documentation

  - Does this pull request introduce a new feature? no, it documents the feature added by PR-1 to PR-3
  - If yes, how is the feature documented? not applicable

They are registered only on the operator that runs the function, under the infix `udf.`, so the identifier is the operator scope (`metrics.scope.operator`) followed by `udf..`. + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + +

Operatorudf.<udf_name>udfProcessingTimeThe time (in nanoseconds) taken by a single invocation of the user-defined function. For asynchronous functions this spans from dispatch to completion. Sampled: only one invocation out of every table.exec.udf-metric.sample-interval is measured.Histogram
udfExceptionCountThe number of exceptions escaping the user-defined function. For synchronous functions this counts exceptions propagating out of eval; for asynchronous functions it counts exceptional completions. Counted on every invocation, not sampled.Counter

This feature is disabled by default. @@ -2441,6 +2471,23 @@ It is recommended to only use them for debugging purposes. If state.ttl is enabled, the size of the value will include the size of the TTL-related timestamp. The value size of AggregatingState is not accounted for because AggregatingState returns a result processed by a user-defined AggregateFunction, whereas currently, only the actual stored data size in the state can be tracked. +## UDF metrics + +Flink can track the processing time and exceptions of SQL/Table user-defined functions on a per-operator basis. This feature is disabled by default. +To enable it you must set `table.exec.udf-metric-enabled` to `true`. When disabled, nothing is registered and there is no overhead. + +Once enabled, each user-defined function gets two metrics on the operator that runs it, scoped under `udf.`: a `udfProcessingTime` histogram and a `udfExceptionCount` counter. + +Flink samples the processing time every `N` invocations, in which `N` is defined by `table.exec.udf-metric.sample-interval`. +This configuration has a default value of 100. A smaller value will get more accurate results but have a higher performance impact since it is sampled more frequently. +Because only the sampled invocations are timed, the remaining invocations cost a single counter increment, so the default interval keeps the overhead of the enabled path small. +Exceptions are counted on every invocation and are not sampled. + +The metrics cover scalar and table functions that a query calls directly, both synchronous and asynchronous. Not covered: Python functions (they run in dedicated Python operators), process table functions (`PROCESS_TABLE`), aggregate functions, functions registered through the deprecated `registerFunction` API, and the functions invoked internally by lookup joins, model prediction, and vector search. + +Warning Enabling UDF metrics may impact the performance, both from the sampled timing and from the metric reporter. +It is recommended to only use them for debugging purposes. + ## REST API integration Metrics can be queried through the [Monitoring REST API]({{< ref "docs/ops/rest_api" >}}).
